Subject: Post-demo: reordering evaluation playbook & SDK/auth checklist

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned.

Recap (what we covered)
- Demo: Redwood SDK + candidate generation -> reranker flow, streaming responses, and structured output for downstream toolbar.
- Key asks from your team: (1) a reproducible reranker evaluation plan, (2) sandbox credentials and an auth model that meets Searchly security needs, (3) guidance on top_k for candidate generation vs reranker window.

Immediate asks / what we need from Searchly
1) Sample query corpus and 1k-2k labeled relevance pairs if available (Searchly_query_set_v1.csv looks like a great start).
2) Target latency SLO (p95) for production queries and preferred top-level metrics (MAP, nDCG, MRR?).
3) Confirmation on whether a short-lived API key is acceptable for the PoC or if you require mTLS/JWT integration from day one.

Our proposed evaluation playbook (high-level)
- Candidate generation: model A (dense embeddings) -> retrieve top 10 candidates per query.
- Reranker: run on top 10, tune reranker top_k output to 3–5 for UX tests. Measure nDCG@5, MRR, and pairwise win-rate.
- Quality baseline: run current Searchly production ranking on the same query set and compute relative lift.

Ownership & next steps
- Vanessa: coordinate PoC timeline, commercial touchpoints, and logistics.
- Karthik: technical onboarding, SDK/auth, and evaluation harness.
- Marissa: SLA/commit and pricing context for Dedicated slot if PoC goes well.

Attachments: redwood-integration-checklist.xlsx (integration checklist), references to Searchly_query_set_v1.csv if you can share an expanded set.

Proposed next meeting: Tue Dec 21, 10:00 PT — 30 minutes to lock scope and credentials. Does that work on your side?

Thanks again,

Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the clear recap. A few clarifying notes and requests from our side: 

- Sample set: attaching Searchly_query_set_v1.csv (sanitized). We can provide a larger unlabeled dump but need a week to sanitize PII.
- Metrics: product cares about top-3 relevance in the UI, but analytics wants nDCG@5 and pairwise A/B comparisons. Can you run both and include precision@3 in the report?
- Latency: initial SLA target is p95 < 150ms for user-facing queries. Internal batch/analytics can be slower.
- Auth: security is asking for short-lived tokens plus audit logs. mTLS would be preferred for Dedicated, but for hosted PoC short-lived API keys are fine if audit logs are captured and retained for 90 days.

One additional ask from Legal (CC’d): we’ll need a short summary of data retention & access patterns for the PoC. Michael, can you confirm which fields need separate encryption?

Hi Sophie / Vanessa — adding technical details and concrete steps for the PoC. Pasted below so your engineers can pick up directly.

1) Sandbox / auth options- Hosted PoC (fastest): short-lived API keys + audit log export (we can push logs to your S3 or to a workspace in your tenant). Keys expire after 24h by default; we’ll extend to 7d for a locked window if you prefer.- Dedicated / production: mTLS or JWT exchanged via your IdP (SAML/OIDC) + KMS-managed keys for any stored artifacts. We support customer-managed KMS for private deployments.

2) SDK onboarding (recommended minimal steps)
- pip install redwood-sdk
- set REDWOOD_API_KEY or configure mTLS cert in SDK client builder
- example retrieve + rerank flow:
  * candidate generation: client.retrieve(model='text-embed-1', queries=..., top_k=10)
  * rerank: client.rerank(model='rerank-v1', candidates=candidates[:10], features=[embedding, score, recency])
  * structured output: set schema via client.parse_schema(...) to get tool-like JSON payloads for downstream UI consumption

3) Routing & model strategy- Route low-latency UI traffic to smaller quantized reranker variants; route nightly reindexing to higher-throughput, higher-cost variants.- Fallback: if reranker capacity limited, serve candidate-gen results (degraded mode) and mark responses with "rerank_applied": false.

4) Evaluation specifics- Holdout: use 2k labeled queries where possible; stratify by query frequency (high/medium/long-tail).- Metrics: nDCG@5 (primary), Precision@3 (UX), MRR (secondary), pairwise win-rate between baseline and candidate pipeline.- Statistical test: bootstrap CIs and paired t-test on per-query nDCG to validate lift.

5) Top_k guidance- Candidate generation: default top_k = 10 for breadth.- Reranker evaluation window: compute reranker scores for the top 10 and tune final output size to 3 for strict UI constraints or 5 if the UX can show more results. For initial tuning, sweep final_k in [3,5] and evaluate nDCG@5 and Precision@3.

6) Quick smoke tests (what I’ll deliver before Tue meeting)- small harness to score your Searchly_query_set_v1.csv against our baseline and a simple reranker variant (results.csv attached in redwood-rerank-smoke-tests.tar.gz).

Notes on data access & retention- For the PoC we will not persist PII in logs by default; query text will be redacted if requested. We can provide a short legal summary for retention and access patterns before the PoC start.

Next steps (owners)
- Vanessa: finalize commercial scope and calendar.
- Sophie: share expanded query dump (best-effort) and confirm retention/encryption requirements.
- Karthik (me): deliver smoke-test artifacts and a runnable SDK example by Mon EOD.

I’ll attach the smoke test bundle and a short readme to the HubSpot record and the Drive link.
